architecture.evidence: Near-identical limiters; X sets the header via res.setHeader (X.diff:65) while Y threads one headers object and drains the body with req.resume() on 429 (Y.diff:72-81) — neither is clearly better against D6.

clean_code.evidence: X is denser (one-line guards/loop, X.diff:11-17) and leaves the existing writeHead untouched; Y is conventionally formatted but restructures the final writeHead (Y.diff:88-89) — a wash.

test_quality.evidence: Tests are line-for-line equivalent except X injects a silent logger (X.diff:87,97) so app tests do not spew request lines; Y's AC-9 predicate (Y.diff:208) is equally strict.

spec_adherence.evidence: Both satisfy AC-1..AC-9 identically (X.diff:89-188 vs Y.diff:111-211); Y's req.resume() (Y.diff:80) is the only behavioural extra and the spec is silent on it.

overall.evidence: Both diffs are the same design with cosmetic differences (X.diff:58-66 vs Y.diff:72-83).

architecture.evidence: Y's load only treats ENOENT as 'missing' and rethrows other read errors (Y.diff:66-69) and commits doc only after the rename succeeds (Y.diff:84-88); X swallows every readFileSync error as 'missing' (X.diff:70) and mutates doc before the write (X.diff:81).

clean_code.evidence: Y extracts load() and names the COUNT regex (Y.diff:64-75,127); X carries a speculative `if (logger)` guard that D6 makes unnecessary (X.diff:75), though Y reassigns its `file` parameter (Y.diff:78).

test_quality.evidence: Y's withApp hands `lines` to the callback (Y.diff:186-193) and tags each invalid-query assertion with the query (Y.diff:310), vs X's out-param `lines = []` third argument (X.diff:177); X's t.mock auto-restore (X.diff:210) is the one point in X's favour over Y's manual restoreAll (Y.diff:239).

spec_adherence.evidence: Both meet AC-1..AC-9; D5 scopes the silent-empty start to a *missing* file, which Y honours via ENOENT (Y.diff:67) while X silently starts empty on any read failure (X.diff:70).

overall.evidence: Y's store.js (Y.diff:53-93) is the one a maintainer can reason about on failure paths; the rest of the two diffs is equivalent.

architecture.evidence: X keeps hashing in auth.js per D4 (X.diff:13-14) and updates the router comment to document `guard?` (X.diff:80); Y moves hashing into keys.findByKey (Y.diff:45), leaves the router comment stale (Y.diff:75) and adds keys-section shape validation D8 never asked for (Y.diff:39).

clean_code.evidence: Y squeezes attach and the store wiring into semicolon one-liners (Y.diff:39, Y.diff:129) where X uses plain blocks (X.diff:38-43, X.diff:137-141); Y's findIndex in remove (Y.diff:62) is the only tidier spot.

test_quality.evidence: X rewrites spec 04's AC-2 pin from 200 to 401 instead of sending a key (X.diff:274-275), silently changing what that test proves; Y mints a key and keeps the 200 assertion (Y.diff:259-270) and dedupes the 401 checks with an `unauth` helper (Y.diff:163-166).

spec_adherence.evidence: Both meet AC-1..AC-10, but X's change to rate-limit AC-2 (X.diff:275) breaks spec 04's locked AC text ('answer the first with 200'), which spec 06's Intent did not license; Y preserves it.

overall.evidence: Y's source is slightly messier (Y.diff:39,129) but its test suite still proves every prior spec's ACs; X's edited pin (X.diff:275) is the kind of quiet drift a maintainer inherits.

note: The strongest difference is in 06-api-keys: when the new auth broke spec 04's rate-limit AC-2 test, diff X changed the expected status of the first GET /todos from 200 to 401 with a comment (06-api-keys.X.diff:275), so the 04 AC is no longer proven as written, whereas diff Y minted a key at module load and kept the 200 assertion (06-api-keys.Y.diff:257-270). In 05, Y's store distinguishes ENOENT from other read failures and commits the in-memory document only after the rename (05-todo-persistence.Y.diff:66-69,84-88), while X swallows any read error as 'missing'. Spec 04's two diffs are the same design with cosmetic differences and most criteria came out unstable across orders.
